## What happened and why the service is down

The deployment has never been healthy. Every attempt to start the `demo` container has been blocked before the container even runs, because Kubernetes cannot satisfy a required environment variable.

[[radar:evidence=0]]

The container spec says: read the value of `GREETING` from the key `GREETING` inside ConfigMap `demo-config`. When Kubernetes went to build the container's environment at startup, it opened that ConfigMap and found no such key. It raised a `CreateContainerConfigError` — meaning "I cannot create this container because its configuration is incomplete" — and has been repeating that failure every time it retries (the Warning event has fired 4 times). Because the container never actually ran, there are no application logs to read.

[[radar:evidence=1]]

Opening the ConfigMap makes the cause concrete: the only key present is `NOTE`, and its value is the comment *"Disposable Radar PR 1265 fixture. The application requires the GREETING key."* The key `GREETING` was never written into the ConfigMap. The deployment and the ConfigMap were created at the same moment (2026-09-21T22:55:06Z), so this is not a regression — the fixture was shipped incomplete from the start.

No other cause is open. Image pulling is not the issue (the Warning event names `CreateContainerConfigError`, not an image error). The container is not crashing at runtime — it has never reached runtime. The ConfigMap itself exists; it is just missing the one key the container needs.

**Fix:** add `GREETING` to `demo-config` with the correct greeting string. The pod will be replaced and the deployment will become Available within seconds. If the ConfigMap is owned by a Helm chart or a GitOps pipeline, make the change there rather than patching the live object, or the next sync will undo it.

Nothing would change this answer — both the deployment spec and the ConfigMap content are unambiguous.
